chapters.1.summary: These are the words of the Preacher, a son of David and king in Jerusalem. He says everything is vapor. He asks what people gain from all their work under the sun. Generations come and go, and the earth stays. The sun rises and sets, and rivers run to a sea that never fills. Nothing is new, and earlier people are forgotten. He set his mind to study all that is done. He found that much wisdom brings much grief.
chapters.2.summary: The Preacher tests pleasure, laughter, and wine. He builds houses, plants vineyards, and makes gardens and pools. He gathers servants, herds, silver, gold, and singers. He denies himself nothing his eyes want. Then he looks at it all and finds it empty. Wisdom is better than folly, yet the wise and the fool both die. He hates his work, since he must leave it to someone else. He concludes that enjoying food and work is a gift from God.
chapters.3.summary: The Preacher says everything has its season. There is a time to be born and to die, to weep and to laugh. There is a time for war and a time for peace. God has made everything beautiful in its time. He has put eternity in human hearts. Yet people cannot find out all that God does. Injustice sits where justice should be, and people die as animals do. The best a person can do is rejoice and do good.
chapters.4.summary: The Preacher looks at the oppression done under the sun. The oppressed weep and have no one to comfort them. He sees that much hard work comes from envy of a neighbor. One handful with quiet is better than two with toil. A man works alone with no son or brother and never asks for whom. Two are better than one, for one can lift the other. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken. A poor, wise youth is better than an old, foolish king.
chapters.5.summary: The Preacher says to guard your steps at God’s house. It is better to listen than to offer a fool’s sacrifice. God is in heaven, so words should be few. A vow to God must be paid without delay. It is better not to vow than to vow and not pay. Whoever loves money never has enough. A worker sleeps well, and a rich man’s plenty keeps him awake. To enjoy food and work is God’s gift.
chapters.6.summary: The Preacher describes a heavy misfortune he has seen. God gives a man riches and honor, and he lacks nothing. Yet God does not let him enjoy them, and a stranger does. A man might have a hundred children and live long. If he finds no good in life, a stillborn child is better off. All a person’s work is for his mouth, and his appetite is never filled. What the eyes see is better than restless desire. No one knows what is good for a person in his few days.
chapters.7.summary: A good name is better than fine perfume. A house of mourning is better to visit than a house of feasting. A wise person’s rebuke is better than the song of fools. Do not ask why the old days were better. In good times be glad, and in bad times consider that God made both. The Preacher has seen the righteous die young and the wicked live long. No one on earth is so righteous that he never sins. God made people upright, and they have looked for many schemes.
chapters.8.summary: Wisdom makes a person’s face shine. The Preacher advises obeying the king, whose word has power. No one has power over the wind or over the day of death. When a sentence for wrong is slow, people grow bold in doing evil. He says it will go well with those who fear God. Yet the righteous sometimes get what the wicked deserve. The wicked sometimes get what the righteous deserve. So he commends joy, and he admits no one can grasp all that God does.
chapters.9.summary: The righteous and the wise are in God’s hand. One fate comes to everyone, and a living dog is better than a dead lion. So eat your bread with joy and enjoy life with the wife you love. Do with your strength whatever your hand finds to do. The race does not always go to the swift. Time and chance happen to all. A poor wise man once saved a small city from a great king. Afterward no one remembered him.
chapters.10.summary: A few dead flies spoil a jar of perfume, and a little folly outweighs wisdom. Fools are set in high places while the able sit low. Whoever digs a pit may fall into it. Whoever splits logs may be hurt by them. A dull ax needs more strength, and skill brings success. A fool talks without end. Woe to a land whose rulers feast in the morning. Do not curse the king even in your thoughts.
chapters.11.summary: The Preacher says to send your bread out on the water. Give shares to seven or eight, since you do not know what trouble may come. Whoever watches the wind will not sow. Whoever studies the clouds will not reap. No one knows the way of the wind or how bones form in the womb. So sow in the morning and keep working in the evening. Light is sweet, and a person should enjoy all his years. The young should rejoice and remember that God will judge.
chapters.12.summary: The Preacher says to remember your Creator while you are young. Hard days will come when the sun and light grow dim. The guards of the house tremble, and the grinders are few. The windows darken, and the doors are shut. People go to their lasting home, and mourners walk the streets. The dust returns to the earth, and the spirit returns to God. The Preacher taught the people and chose his words with care. The conclusion is to fear God and keep his commandments.
